# 12. SEO

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Make the static site crawlable, indexable, useful, and technically clear without manipulative or paid SEO dependencies.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] Unique title tags for every indexable page.
- [ ] Unique meta descriptions for every important page.
- [ ] One descriptive H1 per page unless the page has a documented semantic reason.
- [ ] Canonical links for indexable pages using the final HTTPS production URL.
- [ ] A valid sitemap.xml containing canonical indexable URLs.
- [ ] A robots.txt file that references the sitemap and does not block required assets.
- [ ] Open Graph and Twitter card metadata for share-critical pages.
- [ ] Structured data in valid JSON-LD where it accurately represents visible content.
- [ ] A keyword and intent map tied to real page value, not doorway content.
- [ ] An internal linking model that supports discovery and topical relationships.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Search pages must be written for users first and search engines second.
- [ ] Every indexable page must have unique purpose, content, metadata, canonical URL, and useful internal links.
- [ ] Important content must exist in HTML, not only in images, canvas, or JavaScript-rendered fragments.
- [ ] Metadata must accurately summarize the page and must not promise unavailable content.
- [ ] Structured data must match visible page content and use supported types only where appropriate.
- [ ] Images that contribute to meaning must have useful alt text and crawlable file names.
- [ ] Pagination, archive, and tag pages must avoid thin or duplicate content.
- [ ] SEO must not compromise accessibility, privacy, performance, or brand trust.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check crawlability with internal links, sitemap, robots rules, canonical tags, and production status codes.
- [ ] Check title length, description quality, duplicate titles, duplicate descriptions, and missing headings.
- [ ] Check canonical consistency across tags, sitemap, hreflang, Open Graph URLs, and internal links.
- [ ] Check that no production pages accidentally contain noindex, localhost URLs, draft labels, or blocked assets.
- [ ] Check image alt text, dimensions, compression, filenames, and lazy loading.
- [ ] Check schema JSON parses and does not include fake ratings, fake reviews, or hidden offers.
- [ ] Check that URL slugs are readable, stable, lowercase, and aligned with content.
- [ ] Check that content satisfies intent with proof, detail, and clear next steps.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid doorway pages, city-swap pages, keyword stuffing, hidden text, scraped content, and fake structured data.
- [ ] Avoid relying on paid SEO plugins or proprietary site builders for basic metadata.
- [ ] Avoid canonicalizing many unique pages to the homepage.
- [ ] Avoid blocking CSS, JS, images, or localized pages needed for rendering and indexing.
- [ ] Avoid publishing pages with duplicated placeholder metadata.
- [ ] Avoid treating SEO scores as a substitute for page usefulness.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] A crawler must be able to discover, understand, and prioritize the site's best pages from static HTML alone.
- [ ] Metadata must improve click confidence, not just fill fields.
- [ ] Technical SEO must be boring, consistent, and verifiable.
- [ ] Content quality must be strong enough that SEO work amplifies value rather than masking thinness.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script for titles, descriptions, canonicals, robots, sitemap, headings, alt text, JSON-LD validity, and internal links.
- [ ] Use the fix script to generate sitemap.xml, robots.txt, canonical tags, viewport, charset, and baseline social metadata where safe.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] SEO strategy: clear search purpose, page intent, business alignment, user journey, service/solution/about/case/blog/contact roles, and no duplicate internal intent competition.
- [ ] Site architecture, crawlability, robots, XML sitemap, HTML sitemap, metadata, headings, content quality, keyword/topic mapping, internal links, external links, image SEO, video SEO, schema, local SEO, multilingual SEO, canonicals, performance SEO, mobile SEO, accessibility SEO, social sharing, blog SEO, portfolio/case SEO, service-page SEO, industry/niche SEO, contact SEO, homepage SEO, E-E-A-T/trust, file/assets, redirects/URL consistency, analytics/search tools, pre-launch, post-launch, common mistakes, and final approval are all checked.
- [ ] Every important page has unique title, meta description, one visible H1, logical headings, clean URL, canonical, Open Graph/Twitter tags, useful alt text, crawlable internal links, indexability rules, and human-first content.
- [ ] Sitemap excludes test, duplicate, broken, and noindex pages; robots does not block production; canonicals, hreflang, schema, social images, and metadata use live HTTPS URLs.
- [ ] SEO avoids keyword stuffing, doorway/location duplicates, hidden text, fake reviews/schema, staging indexation, localhost canonicals, JavaScript-only navigation, and thin service/blog pages.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
